newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHARES EASE AFTER SOLID START ON OTE TELECOM.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHARES EASE AFTER SOLID START ON OTE TELECOM.

text.p: Greek shares turned back after a solid start on Tuesday and brokers said market sentiment received a boost from the success of the large part-float of OTE telecom which was completed on Friday.
On Monday June 16 the Athens bourse remained closed in observation of the Holy Ghost holiday.
"OTE's second part-float was a success which will have a knock-on effect on stocks across the board," said Yiannis Kalogerakis, broker at ABN AMRO-Axias Securities.
OTE's second part-flotation was oversubscribed three times, forcing global coordinators to size down the allocation to some 245,000 retail investors to 80 shares.
The price that emerged from the book-building process for institutional investors was 6,600 drachmas per share, while that for retail investors was 6,400 drachmas.
The Greek State lowered its stake in OTE's share capital from 92.43 percent to around 80.0, offering a total of 53.4 million shares.

"The market suffered from reduced activity due to a liquidity squeeze as investors prepared for OTE's part-float," Kalogerakis said. "But the surplus liquidity which came about from the reduction in share allottments will inevitably return to the stock market."
"I anticipate considerable interest for stocks related to OTE's sizeable capital expenditure which will be accelerated after the forthcoming 190 billion rights issue," he added.
Starting on June 18, OTE will tap the market with a 7.5 percent, 190 billion drachma rights issue of 31.6 million shares at 6,000 drachmas each.
Brokers continue to keep a wary eye on the rigid core of consumer price inflation and a likely shift of EU policy on employment.

"The only clouds in the sky at the moment are a rigid consumer price index and the likely shift of emphasis on employment issues following the EU summit in Amsterdam which might affect growth in the entire European industrial sector," Kalogerakis said.
Chart analysts said that strong support levels have been established and the market would move upwards but with reduced volatility.

"The index has set 1,565 points as a strong support level which is also crossed by the long-term trend of this year's rally," said Omega Securities in a technical analysis report. "Short-term indicators point to a neutral stance at current levels."

"But given the impact of OTE's part-float on last week's trading volume we believe that the index will move upwards with reduced volatility to the next critical resistance level of 1,673 points, it added.
The Athens general index was 0.30 percent or 4.93 points weaker at 1,620.80 from Friday's 1,625.73 close after 15 minutes of trading, having earlier reached a high at 1,638.96.
Turnover amounted to 1.9 billion drachmas on volume of 0.5 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 71 to 48 with 17 shares unchanged on 136 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 1,111-1,141 drachmas. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were off 130 drachmas at 6,950.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 655.64-697.49 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $78.21-$79.90. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,853-4,080 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $15.38-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 258-291 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
